findings_addressed.how: automatic._review_native: a KeyboardInterrupt from launch_reviewer now checks review.interactive.json; when it exists the automatic-review.json receipt is written at status 'running' (session_id/background_id copied only when the interactive receipt already bound them), the review/interrupted event with REVIEW_RESUME_NOTE is emitted and the interrupt re-raised; an interrupt before the receipt exists, and every other exception, still records needs_reconciliation. review_candidate's running-resume branch reconciles a receipt lacking session_id through the new Pipeline.reconcile_reviewer() (calls sessions.reconcile('review', path, receipt), events 'Reconciling the interrupted reviewer launch; nothing is relaunched' / 'Reviewer session <uuid> reconciled; awaiting review.completion.json'), copies session_id/background_id into automatic-review.json, then continues with _accept_native; a reconcile failure marks the receipt needs_reconciliation with the error. Pipeline.launch_reviewer wraps the best-effort pane attach in `except BaseException`: the 'Reviewer pane not attached: ...' event is recorded for a Ctrl-C too (message falls back to the exception type name) and non-Exception errors are re-raised so the rule above handles them as an interruption, never a launch failure. FakeSessions mirrors InteractiveSessions.reconcile and keeps a native registry independent of the receipts (native_id/background_id; locate matches by background id). Tests: test_interrupt_after_launch_with_a_bound_session_resumes_the_same_reviewer, test_interrupt_inside_the_settle_poll_reconciles_the_reviewer_then_resumes (receipt running, interrupted event, no stop file, no review.json; resume accepts the file, exactly one launch, reconciled event only in the unbound case), test_interrupt_before_the_launch_was_issued_needs_reconciliation, plus the KeyboardInterrupt sub-case in test_pipeline's launch_reviewer test. RUNBOOK 'Interruption' bullet documents the launch window.

automatic._accept_native wraps the post-acceptance runtime.stop_reviewer(): a failure emits review/running 'Could not confirm reviewer stop: <error>; resume retries the stop' and re-raises. review_candidate's succeeded branch (native transport) calls runtime.stop_reviewer() when review.stop.json is absent or its stopped flag is not true (new helper reviewer_stopped) before returning the persisted review. Because LangGraph persists the failed review task's error, drive() also gained reviewer_stop_pending(runtime, state) (review is the only failed pending task, receipt native+succeeded, stop unconfirmed): a resumed drive may re-enter the node (which only retries the stop and launches nothing), while the drive that hit the failure raises REVIEW_STOP_NOTE ('Reviewer stop not confirmed after acceptance: ...; resume retries the stop with: python -m workflow automatic <dir> --live') instead of spinning on the retry in the same loop. Test test_unconfirmed_stop_after_acceptance_keeps_the_verdict_and_is_retried_on_resume: stop_reviewer failing once -> drive raises, receipt succeeded without error, no stop file, event recorded, source HEAD unchanged; second drive attempts the stop again (attempt count 2), review.stop.json stopped true, integrates, still one launch. RUNBOOK 'Stop' bullet documents it.

FakeSessions knobs: reviewer_session_id (the UUID the native registry reports for the reviewer; set to a worker's plan session id for the not-independent case), reviewer_row_after_file (once review.completion.json exists: a dict merged into the located reviewer row, e.g. a different sessionId, or 'missing' for None), reviewer_after_file (callback run right after the completion file is written; used to dirty review-worktree and to rewrite review.diff). New NativeReviewerGraphTests via assert_refused_after_wait (assert_rejected + review.json absent + no decision in the receipt): test_reviewer_identity_changed_after_the_file_is_refused, test_reviewer_that_is_a_worker_session_is_not_independent, test_reviewer_missing_after_the_file_is_refused (knob set to 'missing' right after wait_review returns, since the wait itself refuses a missing reviewer earlier), test_reviewer_worktree_change_is_refused, test_evidence_change_during_review_is_refused; each asserts the exact RuntimeError message in automatic-review.json, receipt blocked, stop_reviewer called once, review.stop.json present, and a further drive raising Non-retryable with exactly one launch. deviations: F2 needed a drive-level change beyond the two spots the finding named: LangGraph persists the failed review task's error, so without reviewer_stop_pending() a resumed drive would refuse with 'Non-retryable graph failure' before ever re-entering review_candidate's succeeded branch. The retry is deliberately not attempted inside the same drive loop (it would spin on a persistently failing stop); the failing drive raises the specific REVIEW_STOP_NOTE error instead of the generic 'Non-retryable graph failure'.

F1: a Ctrl-C inside the best-effort pane attach is recorded ('Reviewer pane not attached: KeyboardInterrupt') and then re-raised rather than swallowed, so the launch-window rule in _review_native marks the receipt 'running' with the bound session; ordinary Exceptions from the attach are swallowed as before. A KeyboardInterrupt before review.interactive.json exists stays needs_reconciliation (with an explicit error text) rather than being treated as 'nothing launched'.
F1: when reconciliation of a receipt without session_id fails on resume, automatic-review.json is marked needs_reconciliation with the error (fail closed) instead of staying at 'running'.

F3: the 'reviewer missing after the file' case sets the FakeSessions knob ('missing') from a wait_review wrapper right after the wait returns, because wait_review itself refuses a missing reviewer ('Native reviewer missing; reconciliation required') before the post-wait guard can be reached; the knob is still the mechanism, the wrapper only chooses the moment.

F3 guard-removal confirmation was done on scratch copies of the package under the session scratchpad (with contracts/, node_modules/ and features/ symlinked) rather than by editing the checkout; the worker-session case fails on the message rather than on 'not raised' because check_review's later 'Independent reviewer identity required' still blocks the run without the guard.

F4/F5: three of the requested cases (print findings, launch failure -> needs_reconciliation, pane attach RuntimeError) were already correct in production and are green on arrival; the red runs for them are the fixture gap (fake executable ignoring findings) and, for F4's negative case, a scratch copy without the schema validation.

F5's 'a further drive raises the reconciliation error' is asserted two ways: drive raises 'Non-retryable graph failure' (the persisted task error is classified before the node is re-entered) and a direct review_candidate call raises 'Prior reviewer invocation needs reconciliation; no automatic relaunch'; neither launches.

FakeSessions was restructured more than minimally: inventory/locate now model a native registry independent of the receipts (native_id/background_id, locate by background id like InteractiveSessions) so that a receipt stripped of session_id can be reconciled; existing tests still pass.
